about: The grounds every vector names. This is the shape issue #5 §5.4 de-globalizes into a `Ground` descriptor: a case that names its ground here is a case that has declared its inputs. Four grounds are hand-derived — the squares and the sphere every vector was worked out on — and two are read from the public corpus bundles under testdata/corpus/bundles/, so the descriptor a test stands on is the declaration a reader really meets. Both lanes consume this file: analysis/test/vectors.test.ts and tests/cells/conformance_test.go.

reads.tileGridSize: the volume's tile grid size — the world square, the last fallback for the surface
reads.lens.surface: the lens's declared surface, preferred when present
reads.lens.bounds: its raster window, used when no surface is declared
reads.world.attrs: the semconv geometry keys: atlas.geometry.surface and the projection's px/deg mapping
reads.surfaceExtent: derived: [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] in OL world coordinates, x east and y negative-down. Recorded so a candidate carrying the ground differently still has to land on these numbers.
reads.systems: derived: which systems will divide this ground, in the navigator's order.

test/square-1024.about: The unit square of the hand-derived suite: a 1024 world declaring the whole of itself as its lens surface, and no geometry attributes at all — the plane every geohash number in the suite was halved out of.

test/square-1024-bounds.about: The same world with a lens that declares no surface, only a raster window: the fallback branch of surfaceExtent.

test/square-1024-no-lens.about: The same world with no lens at all: the last fallback, the whole world square.

test/sphere-8192x4096.about: The hand-derived sphere: the top half of an 8192 world square declared as a whole equirectangular ground. The S2 vectors — leaf 0x47a1cbd595522b39 and its level-10 parent 47a1cb — are the Go library's own, read through this declaration.

bend-or/2026-08-02/0.about: Bend, Oregon — 2026-08-02, lens "Basemap". Read from the public corpus bundle at testdata/corpus/bundles/bend-or: a plane city that declares an earth Mercator window and names its body, so geohash divides it FOR REAL — genuine WGS84 addresses of the pictured ground, base depth 4 and floor 6 from the window's own 0.32909 x 0.23650 degree spans — and nothing else offers to.

mars/global/0.about: Mars — Global, lens "Viking MDIM 2.1". Read from the public corpus bundle at testdata/corpus/bundles/mars: the one shipped sphere, so the S2 answers here are answers about a declaration a reader really meets.
